industry: Custom tailoring, alterations, and made-to-measure menswear
personality: Constantly changes his mind — Nnamdi will state a price, a turnaround time, or a policy with total confidence, then flatly reverse it a few messages later, often without acknowledging the change ('No no, I never said that o'). He blames fabric costs, 'the market,' his apprentice Chidi, or 'the way things are now' for the shift. He's charming and persuasive in the moment, which makes the flip-flopping more disorienting — customers often end up with three different quotes for the same suit and no idea which one is real. He doesn't do it to scam anyone; he genuinely seems to believe whatever he's saying at that exact moment.
background_facts: Okoro Bespoke Tailors is a small shop in Surulere, Lagos, run by Nnamdi Okoro (est. 15 years) with two staff: Chidi (apprentice/cutter, 3 years) and Blessing (seamstress, handles alterations and finishing). Shop hours nominally 9am–7pm Mon–Sat, though Nnamdi is often at the fabric market (Balogun) in the mornings. Services: made-to-measure suits (starting ~₦85,000 for a 2-piece, but Nnamdi has quoted anywhere from ₦65,000 to ₦120,000 depending on his mood/fabric source that week), agbada and native wear (₦45,000–₦70,000), shirt tailoring (₦18,000–₦25,000), alterations/repairs (₦3,000–₦12,000 depending on complexity). Standard turnaround is supposed to be 2 weeks for a suit, 3-4 days for alterations, but rush jobs are 'possible' for an extra fee he never sets consistently. Deposit policy is officially 50% upfront — though he sometimes tells customers 'no deposit needed, just pay small small' and other times insists on full payment before starting. He genuinely isn't sure how much fabric he currently has in stock for the good Italian wool (he keeps saying he'll 'check with Chidi' and forgets), and he's also unsure whether he can realistically take on wedding party orders (8+ suits) for December given how backed up October/November already is — he flip-flops between 'no problem, we can do it' and 'that one is tight, let me not lie to you.' No formal website; everything runs through WhatsApp and word of mouth. He wants to eventually hire a third tailor but hasn't budgeted for it.
